    How to read this

    Language

    How safe is the way back?

    Comfortable – at least two separate chances to get home after you finish; the last one leaves at least your safety margin later (and the one before it at least half of it).
    Tight – the last departure has your margin, or two chances with half of it. A place with only one chance to get home carries the flag Only one departure.
    Risky – a way back exists but you would have little margin.
    No way back – nothing leaves after your planned finish (hidden by default).
    • Departures less than 10 minutes apart count as one chance (miss one, miss both).
    • A stay that ends within 45 minutes of sunset is capped at Tight, and one that ends after sunset at Risky. Sunset is for flat ground; in the mountains it gets dark earlier.
    • The safety margin is in Filters (default 1 h). Lowering it makes every verdict less cautious. Times are exact for the chosen date: school days, public holidays and seasonal trips are in the data.

    What is included

    • Direct or one change. A journey is a bus or train that goes to Trento (direct), or a bus or train between Trento and a hub plus one local bus that does not call at Trento – that is how you reach Molveno (change at Mezzocorona or Mezzolombardo), Predazzo, Moena or Canazei (change at Cavalese) and many more. Two or more changes are not covered. Choose Direct only in Filters to hide changes.
    • Changes need time: at least 6 minutes on the way there and 10 on the way home (plus the walk when the two stops differ; stops up to 250 m apart count as one hub), and at most 90 minutes of waiting. A late first bus can still make you miss the second one: leave a spare connection on the way home. Journeys that end on the same last bus count as one chance.
    • The plan uses the earliest-arriving departure after your start time. In the place view, pick another departure to see what it would mean.
    • A stop or station is not a trailhead: check the walking time on the map (hiking trails layer).
    • Fast and high-speed trains (RV, EC, AV…) can need another ticket than regional trains; replacement buses carry no bikes.
    • Always check strikes and service changes on the official sites (Trentino Trasporti, Trenitalia) before you go.

    Where the times come from

    • Buses and the Trento–Malè railway: Trentino Trasporti open data (GTFS, CC BY 2.5), official site & service notices.
    • Brenner-line trains (Verona – Trento – Bolzano): STA South Tyrol open data (CC0). Valsugana line (Trento – Pergine – Borgo – Bassano): Trentino Trasporti’s timetable PDFs.
    • Train times are only in the data until 12 Dec 2026. On the Valsugana line some runs are replacement buses (line B450, marked ⇄), and Sunday works can replace trains for a few hours – announced only a few days ahead.
